samples.summary: Cell-block traversal duplicated instead of reusing `model/range-slices.ts`, the module that exists to be the single answer to "which blocks does this range cover"
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` now grows its own cell branch: `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)` → `resolveNestedTableLayout(...)` → `resolved.dataBlock.tableData.rows[..].cells[..]` → `sliceBlockRange(cell.blocks, ...)`. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` states its purpose explicitly — "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers… Rather than keep two copies of the dispatch in sync, both sides drive this module" — and its `visitRangeSlices` already handles exactly these cases (same block, cross-block inside one cell, top-level cross-block), against `doc.blockParentMap`, which is the merged body+header+footer map (range-slices.ts:160-190). The branch justification recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:235-237 ("deliberately not nested-table-aware, so it would reintroduce #872 one level deeper") does not hold for the same-cell branch: it resolves the owning table with `doc.findBlock(anchorCI.tableBlockId)`, and `Doc.findBlock` recurses through nested cells (document.ts:193-238). Concretely, the copy path and the style read/write path now answer "which blocks does this range cover" from two different substrates (layout vs doc), which is precisely the divergence that produced this diff's own header/footer bug (`getLayout()` vs `getActiveLayout()`) — a bug the doc-based traversal cannot have because it never consults a layout.

samples.summary: Read-only image selection, three-layer resize gating, hover gating and hyperlink-click restoration are behavioural scope beyond either issue's acceptance criteria
samples.evidence: Removing `if (readOnly) return;` from `handleImageMouseDown` opens a new viewer-visible interaction (click-select, border-only overlay via `DocCanvas(canvas, readOnly)` + `drawImageSelection(..., { handles: false })`), which in turn forces the `readOnly` gates in `handleImageResizeMouseMove`/`handleImageResizeMouseUp`/`handleImageHover` and the new public `TextEditor.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` to restore link-following on hyperlinked images that `stopImmediatePropagation()` had just taken away. None of this is required by the recorded criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:51-70), whose read-only item is only "Read-only Copy is offered in the context menu **for a text selection** — that always worked." It is a change to documented viewer behaviour (docs/design/sharing.md) that arrived as a side-effect of justifying a focus call, not as a requested outcome. It is documented and works, so the cost stays inside the codebase, but it materially enlarges the change's blast radius relative to the issues.

samples.summary: The stale-image-selection fix is an unenforced "every mutator must remember to call me" rule spread over ~15 call sites plus one outside the module
samples.evidence: `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` must now be called by `insertLink`, `applySpellSuggestion`, `insertTable`, `deleteTable`, `insertTableRow/Column`, `deleteTableRow/Column`, `mergeTableCells`, `splitTableCell`, `insertImage`, `insertPageNumber`, plus `TextEditor.handleCut`/`applyPastePlan`, plus direct assignments in `undoFn`/`redoFn`/`resetAfterDocumentReplace`, plus `DocsFindBar` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:121,133`) for `FindReplaceState`. Nothing enforces the rule; a new mutator silently reintroduces the defect, and the doc itself has to end with "Any future consumer that drives `FindReplaceState`, or the `Doc` directly, owes the same call" (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:353-359). A structural alternative exists in-tree — the selection is already re-validated lazily at every read (`getSelectedImage`, `imageSelectionProvider`, `deleteSelectedImageInline` all do `findBlock` + `findImageAtOffset`), and `invalidateLayout()`/`markDirty` are existing funnels every one of these mutators already passes through. This is also a pre-existing bug class unrelated to #870/#872 except for cut's text path.

samples.summary: Design doc's own hook table contradicts the prose: `imageSelectionClearer` is documented "Cut only" but is also the paste funnel's clearer
samples.evidence: The class snippet reads `/** Drops the image selection without touching the document. Cut only. */ imageSelectionClearer`, while line 319-320 of the same document says it is "wired into `handleCut` and `applyPastePlan` — the single funnel all paste paths reach", which matches the code (`text-editor.ts` `applyPastePlan` calls `this.imageSelectionClearer?.()`). The same stale "Cut only" wording appears on the field's JSDoc neighbourhood in `text-editor.ts`. A reader who trusts the table will not know pastes depend on the hook.

samples.summary: A copied image is written only in the app-private MIME plus alt text, so "copy the image" does not produce anything pasteable outside the app
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` sets `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` and `text/plain` (`image.alt ?? ''`) only — no `text/html` `` flavour and no image blob. Within wafflebase the round-trip works (tested), but the user-facing framing of #870, especially the read-only share-link viewer motivation added in sharing.md ("Clicking an image selects it, so a viewer can copy it"), suggests a viewer expects to paste the image into another app, where they will get an empty string or the alt text. Not listed as a non-goal in docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md's Non-Goals, and not recorded as deferred in the task doc.

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion was amended in-flight to describe the implementation rather than the requirement
samples.evidence: Criterion 1 now reads "Copying a styled range inside a table cell carries inline styles — in the body **and** in a header or footer. The criterion was written unqualified but held only in the body until the copy path was moved from `getLayout()` to `getActiveLayout()` (review finding)". Editing the acceptance list to record what the change ended up doing blurs the spec/implementation boundary; the header/footer extension is legitimate work but reads better as an added criterion or a follow-up than as an annotation on the original one.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out in full. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` declares itself "the one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers", and `visitRangeSlices` (range-slices.ts:145-226) implements the same-block, cross-block-inside-one-cell (162-190, via `doc.blockParentMap` + `doc.findBlock` + `cell.blocks`), and top-level cross-block cases. `getSelectedBlocks()` (text-editor.ts:3783-3816) re-implements that dispatch against a different substrate: `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)` (3804), `resolveNestedTableLayout(cellInfo.tableBlockId, layout)` (3808), `resolved.dataBlock.tableData.rows[..].cells[..]` (3809-3810), `sliceBlockRange(cell.blocks, ...)` (3812), falling back to `layout.blocks` (3815). `doc.blockParentMap` is the merged body+header+footer map (editor.ts:1391-1398) and `Doc.findBlock` recurses through nested cells (document.ts:193-229), so the recorded justification in docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:235-237 is at least weakened for the same-cell branch; that same doc records the range-slices re-base as "still not done", i.e. the repo itself treats this as an outstanding duplicate traversal. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and duplication/reuse is squarely in this lens's lane. The only arguable point is severity (visitRangeSlices yields slices, not cloned blocks, and is documented as non-recursive over nested tables, so straight reuse would need extending), which is a consequence judgement, not a concrete refutation — so the finding stays.
